name: Obinutuzumab
drug_class: Glycoengineered type II anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody
route_note: IV infusion, with loading doses in the first cycle

discovery.note: Humanised type II anti-CD20 IgG1 with a glycoengineered, low-fucose Fc that increases binding to FcγRIIIa. Year of the first published description (GA101; Mössner et al., Blood 2010).

tagline: Glycoengineered type II anti-CD20 antibody with enhanced ADCC for CLL and lymphoma
summary: Obinutuzumab is a humanised, glycoengineered anti-CD20 antibody designed to kill B cells more effectively than rituximab. It is used in chronic lymphocytic leukaemia and follicular lymphoma and, from 2025 in the US, in lupus nephritis.
mechanism: Obinutuzumab binds CD20 in a type II manner: it induces strong direct cell death and does not cluster CD20 into lipid rafts, so complement activation is weaker than with rituximab.
Its Fc carries less core fucose, increasing affinity for FcγRIIIa on NK cells and macrophages and enhancing antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and phagocytosis.
uses: Previously untreated CLL (with chlorambucil or venetoclax)
Follicular lymphoma (first line with chemotherapy, then maintenance; and rituximab-refractory disease with bendamustine)

history.title: Roche acquires GlycArt
history.detail: Roche buys GlycArt and its glycoengineering technology.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in November with chlorambucil for untreated CLL (CLL11), the first approval of a drug with breakthrough therapy designation.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Approved in the EU as Gazyvaro.

history.title: Follicular lymphoma
history.detail: Approved with bendamustine for rituximab-refractory FL (GADOLIN).

history.title: First-line FL
history.detail: Approved for previously untreated advanced FL (GALLIUM).

history.title: Venetoclax combination
history.detail: Approved with venetoclax as fixed-duration first-line CLL therapy (CLL14).

history.title: Lupus nephritis
history.detail: FDA approves obinutuzumab for adults with active lupus nephritis (REGENCY).

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

safety.boxed_warning: Hepatitis B virus reactivation and progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy.

facts: Gazyva was the first drug approved by the FDA under breakthrough therapy designation.
Infusion reactions are frequent with the first dose, which is often split over two days in CLL.

references.title: Roche: FDA approves Gazyva for lupus nephritis (October 2025)
